name: multiply_32_bit_values
description: Multiplies two 32-bit register values by splitting each into 16-bit halves and summing the cross products with the low-half product, which yields the low 32 bits of the full product. The second operand is passed back unchanged in the low word of the 64-bit return value.

name: open_library_and_store_entry
description: Opens a file through the dos open wrapper and, when that succeeds, calls library vectors to look up an entry whose index and pointer are stored in the caller's record. The WINDOW and icon.library text references identify the library being queried, and the file handle is closed at the end.

name: format_text_to_buffer_long
description: Stores the caller's output pointer in a global slot, runs a printf-style formatter with a byte-output callback, the format string and the argument list, then writes a terminating zero at the stored position. It returns the formatter's 32-bit result.

name: format_text_to_buffer_word
description: Stores the caller's output pointer in a global slot, runs a printf-style formatter with a byte-output callback, the format string and the argument list, then writes a terminating zero at the stored position. It returns the formatter's result as a 16-bit value.

name: append_byte_to_buffer
description: Writes the low byte of its argument at the current position of a global output pointer, advances that pointer by one and returns the byte. It has the signature of the single-byte output callback that the formatter routines call.

name: call_two_subroutines
description: The decompiler timed out, so only the listing facts are available: eight instructions that call two other routines and are reached through a pc-relative address and a direct call. No body behaviour can be recovered from the evidence.

name: format_word_digits_by_flag
description: Reads a 16-bit value as signed or unsigned depending on a flag in the caller's record, then calls a helper to extract each digit and writes the digit characters from a lookup table backwards into a buffer. A minus sign is written at the front when a negative signed value is detected.

name: format_signed_word_digits
description: Always reads its value as a signed 16-bit number and extracts digits through a helper and a digit lookup table, filling a buffer from the end. A minus sign is prefixed when the value is negative.

name: parse_printf_format_string
description: Walks a printf-style format string, copying literal characters through an output callback. For each percent directive it reads flags, field width, precision and length modifiers, handles the c, s, d, o, u and x conversions with padding, and returns the count of characters written or -1 when a callback fails.

name: resume_printf_format_parse
description: Resumes the printf-style directive parser at its loop head, reading flags, width, precision, length modifiers and the conversion letter from the format string. It writes padded output through a character callback and returns the number of characters written, or -1 on failure.

name: read_printf_width_digits
description: Accumulates decimal field-width digits from the format string into the width slot, then reads an optional precision after a dot (a star takes it from the argument list). It then reads length modifiers and dispatches on the conversion letter.

name: read_printf_precision_digits
description: Reads the precision digits after a dot in a printf-style format string, taking them from the argument list when a star is given. It then reads length modifiers and dispatches on the conversion letter.

name: resume_printf_precision_digits
description: Continues accumulating precision digits from the format string after the first digit has already been read. It then reads length modifiers and dispatches on the conversion letter.

name: dispatch_printf_conversion_letter
description: Chooses the output path from the conversion letter in a printf-style format string: c, s, d, o, u or x. It then emits the matching argument through the shared padding and output-callback code.

name: emit_printf_octal_value
description: Sets the radix to 8, fetches the next argument, converts it to digits and emits them through the output callback with width, precision and sign padding. It shares its body with the other printf-style numeric emitters.

name: emit_printf_unsigned_decimal
description: Sets the radix to 10, fetches the next argument, converts it to unsigned digits and emits them through the output callback with width and precision padding. It shares its body with the other printf-style numeric emitters.

name: emit_printf_hex_value
description: Sets the radix to 16, fetches the next argument, converts it to digits and emits them through the output callback with width and precision padding. It shares its body with the other printf-style numeric emitters.

name: emit_printf_signed_decimal
description: Marks the conversion as signed decimal, fetches the next argument, converts it to digits and emits them through the output callback with a leading sign and width and precision padding. It shares its body with the other printf-style numeric emitters.

name: emit_printf_string_value
description: Takes the next argument as a null-terminated string, measures its length and emits it through the output callback, honouring the precision limit and width padding. It shares its body with the other printf-style emitters.

name: emit_printf_char_value
description: Takes the next argument as a single character, stores it in a one-byte work buffer and emits it through the output callback with width padding. It shares its body with the other printf-style emitters.

name: select_printf_conversion_handler
description: Selects the output handler for a printf-style conversion by comparing the conversion letter against the cases c, s, d, o, u and x. It calls the shared padding and digit emitters through the output callback and returns the running character count.

name: emit_printf_padded_field
description: Emits a printf-style field through the output callback while tracking the field width and precision limit held in the frame. It calls the padding and character helpers for each character it writes.

name: emit_printf_space_padding
description: Writes the remaining field-width padding through the output callback, decrementing the width counter until it is used up. It stops early and returns an error marker if a callback fails.

name: emit_printf_padding_character
description: Sends one padding character through the output callback and increments the running character count, returning an error marker if the callback fails. It is the single-character step used by the padding loops.

name: count_printf_output_character
description: Increments the running character count in the frame and then emits padding characters while the remaining width allows. It is the counting step of the printf-style padding logic.

name: emit_printf_string_characters
description: Writes the characters of the current string argument through the output callback until a zero byte is reached, counting each one. It returns an error marker if a callback fails.

name: emit_printf_string_with_limit
description: Writes characters of the current string argument through the output callback while the precision limit allows, then fills any remaining width. It counts each character written and returns an error marker on callback failure.

name: emit_printf_zero_padding
description: Emits the zero-padding characters required by a printf-style numeric field through the output callback, counting each one. It returns an error marker when a callback fails.

name: emit_printf_trailing_padding
description: Writes the trailing padding after a printf-style field through the output callback, then returns the running character count. The listing shows the padding loop and the count update only.

name: copy_printf_literal_text
description: Copies the literal characters of a printf-style format string to the output callback until it reaches a percent sign or the end of the string. It counts each character sent and returns an error marker when a callback fails.

name: run_printf_format_loop
description: Runs the top-level loop of the printf-style formatter, copying literal text and dispatching each percent directive until the format string ends. It returns the total character count, or an error marker when a callback fails.

name: return_printf_character_count
description: Returns the 16-bit character count held in the formatter frame. The listing has only two instructions and no other work.

name: negate_result_by_operand_sign
description: Records whether the two signed inputs have opposite signs, calls an unnamed helper for the magnitude, and negates that helper's result when the signs differed. It returns the result paired with the second input in the low word.

name: negate_helper_result_if_negative
description: Calls an unnamed helper and negates its result when the first input is negative, returning the value paired with the second input. The entry is reached only through an unreached gap, so it is a fragment with no further detail.

name: return_helper_result_pair
description: Calls an unnamed helper with no arguments and returns its second register result together with the original second input in a 64-bit pair. It adds no other processing.

name: stub_self_call_thunk
description: Calls its own entry once and then returns, so the listing shows a self-call with no base case and no other work. It is a stub and does not implement a further behaviour.

name: divide_32_by_16_bits
description: Performs unsigned restoring division of a 32-bit dividend by a divisor using a sixteen-step shift-and-subtract loop with carry. It returns the quotient and remainder as a 64-bit pair.

name: divide_by_swapped_word_halves
description: Swaps the two 16-bit halves of the second input and then runs the same sixteen-step shift-and-subtract division on the first input. It returns the quotient and remainder as a 64-bit pair.

name: test_helper_result_bit
description: Calls an unnamed helper through a library vector with a zero and a mask value, then tests one bit of the result. When the bit is set it returns the result if a stored word is zero, otherwise it calls the unnamed routine and returns zero.

name: stub_call_then_return_zero
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns zero, with no other work in the listing.

name: chain_global_result_to_output
description: Calls one helper with the address of a global variable and the constant four, passes its returned value to a second helper, then calls a third unnamed routine. The helpers are the dos output and write wrappers, so the routine is an output step.

name: call_optional_hook_then_run
description: Calls the function pointer stored in a base-relative field when that pointer is non-zero, then calls an unnamed routine and returns. It takes no arguments.

name: release_table_and_handles
description: Walks a table of six-byte entries calling an unnamed routine for each one, then releases the table itself. It also runs an optional callback and calls the stored handle helpers for several saved values, using the exec supervisor and library vectors in the final cleanup.

name: close_table_entry_by_index
description: Looks up a six-byte table entry by index and fails with status 2 and minus one when the index is negative, out of range, or the entry's handle is zero. Otherwise it closes the handle through the dos close wrapper unless a flag bit is set, then clears the entry and returns zero.

name: call_dos_close_function
description: Loads the dos library base from a global variable and calls the Close function at offset minus 36 of that base, returning its result. The listing contains only this one call.

name: call_dos_delete_file_function
description: Loads the dos library base from a global variable and calls the DeleteFile function at offset minus 72 of that base, returning its result. The listing contains only this one call.

name: call_dos_open_function
description: Loads the dos library base from a global variable and calls the Open function at offset minus 30 of that base, returning its result. The listing contains only this one call.

name: call_dos_seek_function
description: Loads the dos library base from a global variable and calls the Seek function at offset minus 66 of that base, returning its result. The listing contains only this one call.

name: call_dos_write_function
description: Loads the dos library base from a global variable and calls the Write function at offset minus 48 of that base, returning its result. The listing contains only this one call.

name: call_library_function_414
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 414 of that base. The listing contains only this one call.

name: allocate_record_with_handle
description: Calls an unnamed helper with minus one and returns zero if that fails. Otherwise it requests a 34-byte block with the flag value 65537 and fills the record's fields from the arguments, a type byte of 4, and the low byte of the first helper result, then passes the record or its embedded field to a further helper.

name: release_and_reset_record
description: If the pointer at offset 10 is set, calls an unnamed release routine on the record first. It then sets the byte at offset 8 and the long at offset 20 to all ones, calls a helper with the byte at offset 15, and calls another routine with the record and the constant 34.

name: forward_with_constant_48
description: Calls an unnamed routine passing its argument and the constant 48, then returns. It adds no other processing.

name: forward_argument_to_helper
description: Calls an unnamed helper with its single argument and returns. It adds no other processing.

name: allocate_type5_record
description: Returns zero when the first argument is zero. Otherwise it allocates a record through a helper with the flag value 65537, sets its type byte to 5, stores the upper word of the second argument and the first argument in it, and returns the record, or zero if allocation failed.

name: reset_record_and_forward
description: When the argument is non-zero, sets the record's byte at offset 8 and the longs at offsets 20 and 24 to all ones, then calls an unnamed helper with the argument and the word at offset 18. It returns that helper's result, or zero for a null argument.

name: reset_record_fields_and_call
description: Sets the byte at offset 8 and the longs at offsets 20 and 24 to all ones, then calls an unnamed routine. It takes no arguments and returns nothing.
